claim: DFW's Q2 2026 departure rate rose about 1% year-over-year and DFW remained the second-worst departure performer among the country's busiest airports, ahead of only Dallas Love Field, in the first full quarter of American's new 13-bank schedule.
source_title: DFW Trails American's Other Hubs in First Quarter of New Schedule
supporting_excerpt: DFW's departure rate rose about 1% year-over-year in Q2. Additionally, DFW remained the second-worst departure performer among the country's busiest airports, ahead of only nearby Dallas Love Field.
units: percent year-over-year change in departure rate
caveat: Trade-press summary; the underlying BTS quarterly data should be validated against BTS Table 6.

claim: American Airlines lengthened scheduled block times on DFW flights, which mechanically improves scheduled on-time performance without changing airborne speed.
source_title: DFW Trails American's Other Hubs in First Quarter of New Schedule
supporting_excerpt: American lengthened scheduled block times on DFW flights to improve on-time performance, noting that since on-time rates are measured against the published schedule, longer block times can improve arrival numbers without changes in actual aircraft speed.
caveat: Trade-press paraphrase of AA disclosure; direct AA operational filings preferred.

claim: American Airlines restructured its DFW schedule from 9 to 13 banks per day starting April 2026.
source_title: American Prioritizes Operational Improvement With DFW Hub Changes
supporting_excerpt: American Airlines is adjusting its bank structure at its central hub from nine to 13 banks per day.
caveat: Analysis blog; cross-corroborated by AA press release and Dallas News.

claim: American's DFW hub operates roughly 930 average peak daily departing flights and 100,000 peak daily customers.
source_title: American Airlines' answer for streamlining traffic at DFW is 'less congestion'
supporting_excerpt: American's DFW operation is evolving to a 13-bank structure, providing more certainty to the airline's average 100,000 peak daily customers traveling on the more than 930 average peak DFW daily departing flights.
units: flights and passengers per peak day
caveat: Peak-day figures, not annual average. Source cites AA's own COO framing.

claim: Wake turbulence recategorization delivered up to 22 additional arrivals per hour at Memphis International Airport (the first RECAT implementation in 2012), roughly a 20% peak-capacity boost.
source_title: FAA Allows Jets To Fly Closer Together With New 'Recat' Rules
supporting_excerpt: Wake turbulence recategorization resulted in a 20% boost in airport capacity, allowing airports to accept up to 22 more arrivals per hour, as demonstrated at Memphis International Airport, the first to implement these new rules in 2012.
caveat: Memphis-specific; DFW mix differs. Cited as reference for RECAT magnitude, not DFW forecast.

claim: MIT Lincoln Laboratory's DFW-specific analysis estimated $4.7 million per year in savings from reducing wake separation from 110 seconds to 90 seconds on arrival, and a +3.5 arrivals per hour improvement on runway 35C from combined wake and runway-occupancy-time reductions.
source_title: Potential benefits of reducing wake-related aircraft spacing at the Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport
supporting_excerpt: Simulation revealed savings of $4.7 million per year when separation criteria was reduced from 110 seconds to 90 seconds ... After runway occupancy time reductions and with the application of reduced wake separation criteria, the arrival-only capacity of DFW runway 35C improved by 3.5 arrivals per hour.
caveat: Simulation-based, not observed. Airport mix and procedures have evolved since publication.

claim: The FAA's 2018 DFW Airport Capacity Profile listed wake recategorization as a future improvement to enhance runway delivery accuracy.
source_title: DFW Airport Capacity Profile
supporting_excerpt: Per search summary of the FAA document: wake recategorization was listed as a future improvement that could enhance runway delivery accuracy at both north and south flow operations.
caveat: Direct PDF fetch was blocked (HTTP 403); claim rests on search-engine summary of the same FAA PDF. Verify against FAA-issued paper copy before citing verbatim.

claim: EUROCONTROL's Airport Collaborative Decision Making (A-CDM) impact assessment across 17 fully implemented CDM airports reported significant reductions in taxi time, fuel burn, flow-management delay, and gate-change churn, and improved ground-handling resource utilization.
source_title: Airport collaborative decision-making (A-CDM) impact assessment
supporting_excerpt: significant reductions in taxi time, fuel burn and flow management delay as well as improved ground handling resource utilisation, a reduction in the number of late stand and gate changes and increased peak departure rates.
caveat: Landing-page text; the underlying 15 MB PDF contains the detailed numbers I did not fetch.

claim: Over 34% of ECAC (European) departures now originate from a CDM airport.
source_title: Airport collaborative decision-making (A-CDM) impact assessment
supporting_excerpt: over 34% of ECAC departures now originate from a CDM airport.
caveat: Vintage figure; current share likely higher.

claim: Average taxi-out time savings from A-CDM implementation range between 0.25 and 3 minutes per departure at implemented airports.
source_title: EUROCONTROL Data Snapshot #40 on taxi times
supporting_excerpt: Average taxi-out time savings from A-CDM implementation range between 0.25 and 3 minutes per departure.
caveat: Range depends on airport size, mix, and pre-existing surface management. Not a DFW forecast.

claim: MARS (Multiple Aircraft Ramp System) gates accommodate one widebody aircraft or two narrowbody aircraft at the same stand, giving operators flexibility to swing between widebody and narrowbody use.
source_title: Enhancing Airport Operations: The Power of MARS Gates
supporting_excerpt: A single stand can accommodate either one widebody or two narrowbody airliners giving operators extra flexibility to cope with potential aircraft size changes in the future.
caveat: General ACI-NA overview; specific stand geometries and lead-in requirements vary.

claim: Chicago O'Hare Terminal 5 gates use a MARS configuration to accommodate one widebody aircraft or be easily converted to two narrowbody positions.
source_title: ADB SAFEGATE to provide automated aircraft parking on new Terminal 5 gates at Chicago O'Hare
supporting_excerpt: Terminal 5 gates at Chicago O'Hare will utilize a MARS configuration to accommodate one wide-body aircraft or be easily converted to two narrow-body positions.
caveat: Vendor blog; corroborated by ACI-NA article.

claim: Narrowbody aircraft achieve 30-45 minute turnarounds while widebodies require 60-90 minutes between flights for cleaning, refueling, and catering; legacy carrier long-haul widebody turnarounds run 90 to 180 minutes.
source_title: Why do widebodies take longer to turn around?
supporting_excerpt: Narrowbodies achieve 30-45 minute turnarounds, while widebodies require 60-90 minutes between flights for cleaning, refueling, and catering. Legacy carriers dealing with long-haul widebody aircraft may have turnarounds lasting 90 to 180 minutes.
denominator: turn cycle from on-block to off-block
caveat: Ranges vary by airline, fleet, and destination.

claim: American Airlines' 777 aircraft turn-time variance versus planned was reported at 56%, materially higher than most narrowbody variance in the same dataset.
source_title: Aviation Wrap-Up April 2023
supporting_excerpt: Widebody aircraft performed poorly in comparison to narrowbodies, with American's and United's B777Ws having a 56% and 22% variance, respectively.
units: percent variance from planned turn time
caveat: Independent analyst publication; underlying dataset not disclosed.

claim: DHS Science and Technology's target for next-generation TSA checkpoint lanes is 300 passengers per hour per lane.
source_title: 300 People Per Hour Per Lane
supporting_excerpt: 300 People Per Hour Per Lane (DHS S&T program target for next-generation checkpoint lanes).
denominator: single checkpoint lane at design operating condition
caveat: Program target, not observed field average.

claim: Deployed CTiX checkpoint lanes achieve approximately 200 passengers per hour on average and up to 330 per hour during peak.
source_title: Passenger throughput: how airports can improve performance at the checkpoint
supporting_excerpt: The installation of CTiX scanners has increased throughput to approximately 200 passengers per hour on average and 330 per hour during peak times.
caveat: Vendor source; independent verification against TSA operational data preferred.

claim: Some airports that deployed CT-based checkpoint technology reported wait-time reductions of as much as 30%.
source_title: TSA's New CT Scanners: What Travelers Need to Know
supporting_excerpt: Some airports implementing CT tech have reported a noticeable drop in delays — as much as 30% less wait time for passengers overall.
caveat: Consumer press summary; specific airports and baselines not stated.

claim: DFW's Skylink automated people-mover operates at approximately 2-minute headway with a maximum interterminal transit time of 9 minutes.
source_title: Skylink (Dallas Fort Worth International Airport) — Wikipedia
supporting_excerpt: Trains depart every 2 minutes, with a maximum travel time of 9 minutes between the farthest points.
caveat: Wikipedia; corroborated by DFW airport plan-your-connection guidance.

claim: American's published minimum connection time at DFW is 40 minutes for domestic-to-domestic and 40 minutes for domestic-to-international; connections from an inbound international flight to a domestic flight require significantly longer due to customs clearance.
source_title: DFW Minimum Connection Times [2025]
supporting_excerpt: The DFW minimum connection time for AA domestic to either domestic or international outbound is 40 minutes. However ... For connections from an international flight to a domestic flight at DFW, 2 hours is the minimum time that you would need.
caveat: Consumer-facing summary; the AA-published MCT tables via ATPCO/OAG are the authoritative source.

claim: DFW opened a new nine-gate Terminal C pier constructed with modular technology; six pre-fitted megastructure modules were moved across two closed runways overnight, with mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and fire-protection systems pre-installed.
source_title: DFW Airport Completes Move of Innovative Megastructure Modules Across Airfield for Terminal C Expansion
supporting_excerpt: The engineering feat included moving a total of six massive modules – the largest measuring 204 feet long by 68 feet wide and weighing approximately 1,200 tons – across two closed runways overnight using self-propelled modular transporters. DFW installed mechanical, electrical, plumbing and fire-protection systems in the six modules prior to being transported to the site.
caveat: HOK is the design firm; corroborated by DFW newsroom.

claim: DFW and American opened nine Terminal C gates in June 2026 (4 net-new, 5 rebuilt), pier spans 115,000 sq ft; Terminal C will ultimately deliver 32 gates across more than one million square feet.
source_title: DFW Opens Nine Gates In $3B American Airlines Terminal
supporting_excerpt: The pier expansion delivers 4 net-new gates, as well as 5 gates that were rebuilt as part of the project. ... The new pier housing the nine gates spans 115,000 ft. Terminal C will ultimately deliver 32 gates across more than one million square feet.
caveat: Aviation Week reporting; primary AA/DFW press release should confirm.

claim: American opened its largest Admirals Club to date at DFW Terminal C, approximately 37,000 square feet near the Skylink station.
source_title: Airport Context Packet — DFW Terminal F, 2043 Horizon
supporting_excerpt: Admirals Club (new, Terminal C): Approximately 37,000 square feet near the Skylink station — described by American as its largest Admirals Club to date.
caveat: Airport-context packet references AA public statements; verify against AA newsroom before external citation.

claim: American Airlines' announced Terminal F lounge posture as of the joint program announcement is a Provisions by Admirals Club grab-and-go concept rather than a Flagship-tier lounge.
source_title: Airport Context Packet — DFW Terminal F, 2043 Horizon
supporting_excerpt: Terminal F lounge posture (as announced): A Provisions by Admirals Club grab-and-go concept — a scaled-down offering rather than a Flagship-tier lounge — is planned for Terminal F.
caveat: Airport-context packet references publicly announced plans; may not reflect final buildout.

claim: DFW is jointly owned by Dallas and Fort Worth; American Airlines carried 82.6% of DFW's passengers (70.8 million of 85.7 million) in 2025 and operated 82% of departures; carrier-level connecting share at DFW is around two-thirds and airport-level connecting share is around 60%.
source_title: Airport Context Packet — DFW Terminal F, 2043 Horizon
supporting_excerpt: American Airlines carried 82.6% of DFW's passengers (70.8 million of 85.7 million) and operated 82% of departures. ... DFW-level secondary reporting places connecting share at about 60%. American's own DFW hub materials describe DFW as the airline's largest connecting complex; the run prompt asserts 'two-thirds of American's DFW customers connect.'
units: percent of passengers and departures; percent connecting
caveat: Context packet notes distinction between airport-level and carrier-level connecting share.

claim: Terminal F scope is 31 gates, sole American Airlines occupancy, approximately $4 billion capital cost; first phase operational in 2027, full program targeted for 2030; modular construction with reported approximately 30% cost savings versus conventional construction.
source_title: Airport Context Packet — DFW Terminal F, 2043 Horizon
supporting_excerpt: Scope: 31 gates, sole American Airlines occupancy, approximately $4 billion. Timeline: First phase scheduled to be operational in 2027; full program targeted for 2030. ... DFW and secondary sources report approximately 30% cost savings versus conventional construction.
caveat: Context packet aggregates DFW press-release language; the 30% figure is DFW self-reported.

claim: DFW had 71% on-time departures in 2024, down from 75% in 2023, ranking 30th among major U.S. airports.
source_title: What are the best and worst airports and airlines for on-time performance?
supporting_excerpt: DFW had 71% on-time departures in 2024, down from 75% in 2023, ranking 30th among major U.S. airports.
caveat: USAFacts uses BTS data; verify against BTS Table 6 directly for citations.

claim: Departure-Sensitive Arrival Spacing (DSAS) at LaGuardia can raise departure throughput by up to 9 aircraft per hour with little or no impact on arrivals during peak traffic demand; combined Terminal Sequencing and Spacing plus DSAS can lift departure throughput from a 38/hr baseline to 47/hr at maximum arrival demand.
source_title: Reducing Departure Delays at LaGuardia Airport with Departure-Sensitive Arrival Spacing (DSAS) Operations
supporting_excerpt: DSAS operations have the potential to increase departure throughput at LGA by up to 9 aircraft/hour with little or no impact on arrivals during peak traffic demand period. With maximum arrival demand (40-41 arrivals per hour), departure throughput could be increased from 38/hour (baseline condition), to 44/hour (TSS condition), to 47/hour (TSS + DSAS).
caveat: Simulation-based results; not observed field averages.

claim: American publicly framed the 13-bank restructure as delivering measurable improvements in on-time arrivals and departures, customer connections, and baggage handling in its first two weeks of operation.
source_title: Forever Forward at DFW: Enhanced flight schedule unlocks countless customer benefits
supporting_excerpt: In April, American transformed its schedule from a nine to 13-bank operation, spreading customers and flights throughout the day. The new bank structure has already brought measurable improvements in on-time arrivals and departures, customer connections and baggage handling at DFW.
caveat: Corporate press release; qualitative claim not accompanied by disclosed metrics in the release.

claim: Contact gates are cheaper to operate than remote stands because they avoid bussing and generally allow shorter turn times; remote stands carry secondary transport delays commonly of 20-30 minutes each way.
source_title: Using Remote Stands And Contact Gates
supporting_excerpt: Contact gates are cheaper to operate as they don't require passengers to be bussed and the turn round time is generally shorter. ... passenger processing is slower at remote stands due to the need for secondary transport, with bus transfers commonly taking 20-30 minutes each way.
caveat: Forum-quality source; corroborating figures should be sought from ACI or ACRP for external citation.
